meta.title: Open CAD Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Open CAD Studio: free, open source 2D and 3D CAD that reads and writes DWG and DXF natively. Layouts, plotting to PDF, solids and an AI connection. For Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser. A community project by Hakan Seven.

header.label: Community project · 2D and 3D CAD
header.title: Open CAD Studio
header.tagline: Open source CAD that reads and writes DWG and DXF itself
header.desc: Draft in 2D, model in 3D and lay out on paper, on the desktop and in the browser. Open CAD Studio is built in Rust, renders on the GPU and opens your drawings without a conversion service. An open source project by Hakan Seven and a growing group of contributors, supported and promoted by the OpenAEC Foundation.

notice.text: Try it now: open the web version, drag a DWG or DXF file into the window and browse model space and the layouts. Nothing gets installed.

community.label: Community project
community.title: Made by Hakan Seven and contributors
community.desc: Open CAD Studio was not developed by the OpenAEC Foundation. Hakan Seven started the project in March 2026; by now about eighty people have contributed, the foundation among them. It fits our mission: open software for the whole construction chain, without depending on a single vendor.

license.title: GPL-3.0
license.desc: Free to use, study and change. Note: stricter than the LGPL-3.0 of our own apps if you include the code in your own software.

infra.title: The base for Open Infra Studio
infra.desc: Our plug-ins for GIS and civil engineering run inside Open CAD Studio.

features.label: Features
features.heading: From the first line to a plotted layout
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

dwg.title: DWG and DXF without a detour
dwg.desc: Open, edit and save DWG and DXF directly, and choose a version from R14 up to 2018 when you save. External references, blocks with attributes and a backup or autosave file open as well.

draw.title: Draft the way you are used to
draw.desc: The command line, object snaps and tracking, layers with filters, hatches, tables and dynamic blocks. If you have worked with DWG for years, you will find the commands under their familiar names, also in a classic workspace.

model.title: Solids on a real geometry kernel
model.desc: Extrude, revolve, sweep, loft and Boolean operations, with ACIS solids from existing drawings. The GPU draws large models smoothly, orthographic or in perspective.

auto.title: Plug-ins, scripts and an AI assistant
auto.desc: Extend the app with plug-ins, run command scripts or convert drawings without a window. Through the built-in MCP server an AI assistant can read drawings, draw and take screenshots; the node graph builds geometry without code.

dwg.title: DWG and DXF
dwg.desc: Read and write, with save as R14 up to 2018.

xref.title: External references
xref.desc: Attach, reload and bind xrefs, and write blocks out with WBLOCK.

import.title: Import
import.desc: PDF, DGN V8, SVG, OBJ meshes, raster images and survey points from LandXML.

export.title: Export
export.desc: STL and STEP AP203 for 3D, CSV with object data and IFCCAD as an open drawing format (experimental).

geom.title: 2D drafting
geom.desc: Lines, polylines, arcs, ellipses, splines and revision clouds, with object snaps and tracking.

modify.title: Modify
modify.desc: Offset, trim, extend, fillet, array, mirror and more, also with grips and properties.

layers.title: Layers and filters
layers.desc: A layer manager with filters, groups and layer states, and quick select by property.

hatch.title: Hatches
hatch.desc: Patterns and gradients, with islands, boundaries and annotation scale.

dims.title: Dimensions and text
dims.desc: Dimensions, leaders, tolerance frames, tables and fields, with your own styles.

blocks.title: Blocks with attributes
blocks.desc: Dynamic blocks with parameters, actions and visibility states, and attributes edited in one form.

layouts.title: Layouts and viewports
layouts.desc: Model space and paper space with scaled viewports, page setups and plot styles (CTB/STB).

plot.title: Plot and publish
plot.desc: Layouts to PDF or the printer, several sheets in one PDF, and comparing two drawings.

solids.title: Solids
solids.desc: Box, sphere, cylinder, extrude, revolve, sweep, loft and Boolean operations.

acis.title: ACIS from drawings
acis.desc: 3DSOLID, REGION and BODY objects from DWG and DXF are shown correctly.

gpu.title: Fast on the GPU
gpu.desc: 2D and 3D display through wgpu, also for large drawings with many objects.

mcp.title: Works with an AI assistant
mcp.desc: An MCP server lets an assistant read, edit and capture the drawing.

graph.title: Node graph
graph.desc: Build drawings with nodes for every object the drawing commands make.

plugins.title: Plug-ins and scripts
plugins.desc: Native plug-ins from a registry, command scripts and conversion without a window.

cui.title: Your own workspace
cui.desc: Your own ribbon panels, shortcuts and toolbars, or the classic workspace.

layers.title: New layer manager
layers.desc: Filters stored in the drawing, layer groups, layer states and importing layers from another drawing.

tables.title: Tables

blocks.title: Dynamic blocks
blocks.desc: Flip parameters, value sets and a parameters manager to edit in.

svg.desc: SVG and SVGZ as a block in the drawing, also by drag and drop.

arm.title: More platforms
arm.desc: Builds for Windows and Linux on ARM64 and for Macs with an Intel processor.

cost.a: Nothing. Open CAD Studio is open source under the GPL-3.0: no licence fees, no subscription and no account.

who.a: Hakan Seven is the creator and maintainer. Dozens of developers contribute as well, also from the OpenAEC Foundation. The foundation does not own the project, but supports it and builds Open Infra Studio on it.

dwg.q: Can I use my existing DWG drawings?
dwg.a: Yes. DWG and DXF are read and written directly, without a conversion service, and you choose a version from R14 up to 2018 when you save. The app is still in active development: keep a copy of important drawings and report problems on GitHub.

web.q: What is the difference between the web version and the desktop app?
web.a: Both use the same core. In the browser you open drawings through the browser and save them as a download. The desktop app associates itself with DWG and DXF files, prints, creates PDFs and runs plug-ins, scripts and the MCP server.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows and Linux on x64 and ARM64, macOS on Apple silicon and Intel, and any modern browser. On Windows you can also install it through winget.

update.q: How often is there a new version?
update.a: Every week, usually on Sunday. The version number is the year plus the week number, such as 2026.45. The download buttons on this page always point to the newest version.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: The desktop app has an MCP server. With it an assistant can open drawings, query and create objects, run commands, check and save, and take screenshots of the drawing window. You see everything happen in the app.

lang.q: Which languages is the app available in?
lang.a: In 23 languages, including Dutch, English, French, Turkish and Spanish.
